_comment: How raw text becomes speakable text. Consumed by both halves. Everything here is DATA, not prose: if a field cannot be acted on by a program, it belongs in a key prefixed with an underscore, which consumers must ignore.
_schema: No regular expressions live in this file, deliberately. Python's re and JavaScript's RegExp differ on lookbehind width, named-group syntax, and backreference syntax, so a shared pattern is a shared bug waiting to happen. Instead each rule states a condition from a small fixed vocabulary that both sides implement identically. Adding a condition means changing both engines on purpose, which is the point.

_modes.full: read the entire URL character by character
_modes.domain: read only the domain, e.g. 'link to example.com'

_symbol_conditions.isolated: only when whitespace or a string boundary sits on BOTH sides
_symbol_conditions.digit-before: only when the nearest preceding non-space character is a digit
_symbol_conditions.digit-after: only when the nearest following non-space character is a digit

_symbol_rationale: The conditions are what keep expansion from wrecking real text. Bare substitution turns C++ into 'C plus plus', addresses into 'user at example dot com', and '## Heading' into 'number number Heading'. Each condition below was chosen against a specific way the naive version fails.
_output_contract: Pipeline order: collapse (typographic), then expansions, then currency, then symbols. After the symbol stage, collapse runs of spaces and tabs to a single space and trim the ends. Newlines are left alone. Without this the two implementations produce the same speech from different strings — one pads every replacement, the other pads only where needed — and a cross-language check can then only ever assert equivalence, never equality. It also matters for anything mapping offsets through normalization, where a stray double space shifts every position after it.
_currency_note: Currency symbols are prefixes in text but suffixes in speech: $50 is spoken 'fifty dollars', not 'dollars fifty'. That reordering is why they cannot live in the symbols list above. Applies only when a number follows.
_expansions_note: Say-as expansion lives here, NOT in pronunciation.json. The division: this file decides what a token MEANS when spoken, pronunciation.json decides how a word SOUNDS. Both sides must apply these before the pronunciation dictionary runs.

_expansion_matching.literal: Matches are literal substrings, never patterns. Same reason as the symbols above: shared regexes drift between Python and JavaScript.
_expansion_matching.boundaries: A match is rejected when the character immediately before OR immediately after it is a letter or a digit. This replaces the word-boundary anchors the old regex entries carried. It is what stops 'w/' firing inside 'w/o', and what stops '->' firing inside the C pointer syntax 'node->next' while still catching 'A -> B'.
_expansion_matching.longest_first: Candidates must be tried longest first, so 'w/o' wins over 'w/' and 'et al.' wins over any shorter prefix. Sorting by match length descending at load time satisfies this.
_expansion_matching.case: Matching is case-insensitive by default, which is correct for every entry currently in the list: 'n.b.' and 'N.B.' mean the same thing. Set matchCase true on an entry that would otherwise eat an ordinary word. Nothing here needs it yet, but the first person to add 'US' for United States would silently rewrite every 'us' without it.

expansions._why: prose arrows only; the boundary rule leaves node->next alone

_numbers_note: Flags only. Each side owns the algorithm; this file owns whether it runs. Prose descriptions are here as _examples so neither side has to guess what the flag means.

_examples.years: 1984 reads as nineteen eighty-four, not one thousand nine hundred eighty-four
_examples.phone_grouping: digits grouped in threes with pauses
_examples.versions: v2.1.3 reads as version two point one point three
_examples.large_threshold: at or above this value, 1,200,000 reads as one point two million

_modes.announce: say 'code block, twelve lines' and skip

_collapse_note: Typographic cleanup, applied FIRST, before expansions. It has to run first: every later rule matches literal text, and a curly apostrophe or a soft hyphen sitting inside a word defeats them, and defeats the pronunciation dictionary after them. Measured on the shipped CMUdict, 'don’t' with a curly apostrophe phonemises as 'dawn tee' and 'won­derful' with a soft hyphen as 'wun DERful'. Almost every professionally typeset page uses curly apostrophes, so this was most contractions on most articles.

_collapse_rules.zero_width: Remove U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF. They are invisible and split words for anything matching literal text.
_collapse_rules.soft_hyphens: Remove U+00AD. It is a rendering hint, never a spoken hyphen.
_collapse_rules.smart_quotes_to_plain: U+201C U+201D U+201E U+201F and U+2033 become a straight double quote; U+2018 U+2019 U+201A U+201B and U+2032 become a straight apostrophe. Guillemets are deliberately left alone: they are not English quoting and mapping them would be a guess.
_collapse_rules.nbsp_to_space: U+00A0, U+202F and U+2007 become an ordinary space, which the output contract then collapses. They are not spaces or tabs, so the contract does not reach them.
_collapse_rules.dashes_to_plain: U+2013 en dash, U+2012 figure dash and U+2015 horizontal bar become a hyphen.
_collapse_rules.em_dash_to_comma: U+2014, together with any spaces or tabs on either side of it, becomes a comma and a space. Absorbing the spaces matters: replacing the character alone turns 'left — quickly' into 'left , quickly', with the comma floating away from the word it belongs to. This rule has speech content rather than being cleanup: the engines have no phoneme for a dash and drop it silently, so the pause the author wrote disappears.
_collapse_rules.footnote_markers: Remove superscript digits U+00B9, U+00B2, U+00B3 and U+2070-U+2079. Bracketed markers like [1] are deliberately NOT removed: they are indistinguishable from a citation the reader may want.
_collapse_rules.dot_leaders: A run of four or more periods, optionally separated by spaces, becomes a single space. Table-of-contents leaders, not punctuation. Runs of two or three are left to repeated_punctuation below.
_collapse_rules.repeated_punctuation: A run of two or more of the SAME terminator (. ! ?) becomes one. Applied after dot_leaders, so a leader run is already gone.
_collapse_rules.emoji: 'skip' removes emoji; 'read' leaves them for the engine. Extended pictographic characters, EXCEPT any character that appears in the symbols or currency lists above. That exception is not tidiness: U+00A9, U+00AE and U+2122 are all Extended_Pictographic, so a plain pictographic test deletes the copyright, registered and trademark signs and with them the words the symbols list exists to produce. The lists are the authority on what gets spoken.
_collapse_rules._order: zero_width, soft_hyphens, smart_quotes_to_plain, nbsp_to_space, dashes_to_plain, em_dash_to_comma, footnote_markers, dot_leaders, repeated_punctuation, emoji. Both halves apply them in this order; two of them interact, so the order is part of the contract.
